question.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\sqrt{6}t,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
question.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{7}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{7}) \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{7}),\,2\sqrt{6}\cdot \frac{s}{7},\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{7})⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{7}),\,\frac{2\sqrt{6}s}{7},\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{7})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{7})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2\sqrt{6}s}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{7}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{5}{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{7}),\,\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{7},\,-\frac{5}{7}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{7})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
